headers.description:
File extensions whose contents every compile step depends on, such as
headers no step lists as an input.

paths.description:
The paths the compiler sees. Fixed spellings keep paths that a
compiler writes into its output identical on every machine. Without
this table, Win32 compilers under Wine see `R:\source`, `R:\build`,
`R:\toolchain`, and `R:\Users\reprobit\AppData\Local\Temp`; others
see `/source`, `/build`, `/toolchain`, and `/tmp`.

state.description: Local, ignored working state: builds, caches, and reports.

toolchain.description: The compiler and the tools its steps call.

source.description: Where the project's sources appear, such as `R:\source` or `/src`.

temp.description: The temporary directory the compiler is given.

toolchain.description: Where the compiler's own files appear.

Prelude.description:
A declaration-only prelude. Every family emits declarations that produce
no code, data, or linker directives; they only steer compiler state.

oneOf.description: A grid of classes with `functions` unused inline members each.

args.description:
Arguments. `${SOURCE}`, `${BUILD}`, `${TOOLCHAIN}`, and `${TEMP}`
expand to the compiler-visible roots.

env.description: Extra environment, with the same placeholders as `args`.

inputs.description: Files read, as `source/…` or `build/…` (an earlier step's output).

outputs.description: Files written, relative to the build root.

prelude.description:
Declaration-only text force-included before the source: the
reviewed compiler-state adjustment `rbit grind` finds.

program.description:
A command of the compiler or of a listed tool: `cl`, `objdiff-cli:objdiff-cli`,
or a path inside the compiler such as `Bin/CL.EXE`.

registers.description:
Registers renamed in a function of the step's object after it
compiles, by symbol: `{ _transform = { esi = "edi", edi = "esi" } }`.
A rename permutes `ebx`, `esi`, and `edi` in an i386 function, which
every calling convention preserves, so behaviour cannot change.

artifact.description: The rebuilt file, relative to the build root.

normalize.description:
Metadata normalizations applied to both sides before comparing:
`pe-timestamps`, `pe-checksum`, or `build-id`. Each clears only fields
a linker fills from the clock or a random source.

reference.description:
The original file, relative to the project. Project-owned and never
redistributed; it is read only by verification.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 the reference must have after `normalize`, so a wrong
original is caught before any comparison.

stamp.description:
Values written into the built artifact after the last step, such as
`{ pe-timestamp = 0x3f3a5c1e }` for the original's link time. Unlike
`normalize`, the artifact itself then matches. Each value is declared
here for review; nothing is read from the reference.

Toolchain.description: The tools a project builds with.

compiler.description: Catalog id of the compiler, such as `msvc-4.2` or `decompme/ps2/ee-gcc2.95.3-136`.

runs.description:
Overrides where the compiler runs (`host`, `windows`, `linux-x86_64`, `linux-i386`)
when the catalog's platform-wide guess is wrong for this compiler.

tools.description: Other catalog tools steps may call, by id.
